_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: bivariate normal with rho 0.5; Spearman's value for a bivariate normal is (6 / pi) asin(rho / 2)

agreement.claim: both engines report the same Pearson and Spearman coefficients and intervals
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 at ten significant digits on every key. harness/categorical_examples.test.py checks both coefficients against numpy's corrcoef on the values and on their ranks, the Pearson interval against Fisher's z, and shows Pearson's standard error applied to Spearman gives a different interval.

recovery.claim: each coefficient is close to the value the fixture was built with

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: Measured by harness/categorical_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99 of this generator.
